posts.text: [Image] The image presents a graph comparing real wage growth under President Biden and during former President Trump's second term. It shows a bar chart indicating a total change of -$2,909 for Biden and a positive change of $1,151 for Trump. Additionally, a pie chart illustrates that 39.6% of Biden's real wage loss has been made up, equating to $1,151, while 60.4% remains, totaling $1,758. The source of the data is noted as the Bureau of Labor Statistics and CEA calculations.

posts.text: [Image] The image presents a bar graph comparing capital spending rates under two administrations. The blue bar represents President Joe Biden's projected annualized rate for 2023-2024 at 3.7%, while the red bar shows former President Donald Trump's projected rate for the first half of 2025 at 8.4%. The graph emphasizes the difference in capital spending between the two leaders, highlighting Trump's significantly higher projected rate.

posts.text: [Image] The image presents a bar graph titled "A Manufacturing Renaissance is Under Way," showing the annualized percentage change in total real manufacturing output from the first quarter of 2023 to the second quarter of 2025. The graph features both positive and negative values, with notable increases projected for 2025, reaching 3.5% in Q1 and 2.4% in Q2. The data is sourced from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

posts.text: [Image] The image presents a line graph titled "Consumer Spending is Outpacing Inflation." It displays data from January 2023 to July 2025, with the y-axis representing consumer spending in trillions of chained 2017 USD. The graph shows a steady increase in consumer spending, starting around 10.4 trillion and rising to approximately 12 trillion by mid-2025. The trend indicates that consumer spending is consistently outpacing inflation during this period.

The source of the data is noted as the U.S. Treasury and CEA Calculations.

posts.title: We had a very productive call with President Lula of Brazil. Among the things discussed were Trade, how our Countries could work together to stop Organized Crime, Sanctions imposed on various Brazilian dignitaries, Tariffs, and various other items. President Lula and I established a relationship at a meeting which took place at the United Nations, and I believe it set the stage for very good dialogue and agreement long into the future. I look forward to seeing and speaking with him soon. Much good will come out of this newly formed partnership!
